properties.description: Giant HII region ionised by the Trapezium cluster.
Star-forming region famous for HST "Pillars of Creation".
Massive complex surrounding Eta Carinae LBV system.
Ultracompact HII region hosting dozens of massive YSOs.
Multi-core compact HII complex along the galactic plane.
Diffuse neutral HI cloud enveloping the Solar System.
Archetypal spherical planetary nebula with OIII dominated shell.
Low-surface-brightness near-spherical PN with darker eyes.
Complex bipolar PN with concentric shells and jets.
Extreme bipolar lobes with hot dense equatorial dust torus.
Nearest PN, dominated by thousands of cometary knots.
Irregular asymmetric shell with multiple dust patches.
Classic blue reflection nebulosity around the Pleiades cluster.
Blue reflection nebula illuminated by Rigel.
Iconic dark column silhouetted against IC 434.
Large diffuse dark cloud near the Southern Cross.
Dense dark cloud in the Orion-B complex.
Nearby dense Bok globule completely opaque to background stars.
S-shaped cluster of small Bok globules near Ophiuchus.
Shell-type SNR from an ~10k-year-old supernova.
Type Ia remnant from the SN 1572 observed by Tycho Brahe.
Archetypal pulsar wind nebula energised by the Crab Pulsar.
Inner plerion of the Vela SNR with visible jets.
Classic WR wind-blown shell around the WN6 star WR 136.
Young WR nebula around the runaway WN8h star WR 124.
ALMA-resolved concentric rings and planet-forming gaps.
Nearby face-on protoplanetary disk with ALMA-imaged gaps.
Hot low-density ISM cavity enclosing the Solar neighbourhood.
Giant superbubble in the LMC carved by its OB association.
Ring of overlapping superbubbles in the solar neighbourhood.
Giant HII region in Sagittarius — one of the largest Messier nebulae.
Combined emission + reflection + dark nebula split by dust lanes.
Massive HII region and active star-forming cluster.
Large circular HII region with cluster NGC 2244 at its core.
Dark pillar silhouetted against the HII nebula NGC 2264.
Large faint emission nebula in Perseus ionised by ξ Persei.
Continent-shaped emission nebula near Deneb.
Companion HII region to NGC 7000 across a dark dust lane.
First planetary nebula ever discovered (Messier 1764).
Youngest known galactic SNR (~340 yr); brightest radio source in the sky.
Brightest stellar event in recorded history (1006 AD, mag -7.5).
Last naked-eye Milky Way supernova (1604 AD); likely Type Ia.
Coldest known natural location in the universe (~1 K).
Supermassive black hole at the centre of the Milky Way (~4.3×10⁶ M☉).
Supermassive black hole in M87, imaged by the Event Horizon Telescope in 2019.
First widely-accepted stellar-mass black hole (~21 M☉), discovered 1964.
X-ray binary with a ~9 M☉ stellar black hole primary.
Young pulsar (33 ms) at the heart of the Crab Nebula, SN 1054 remnant.
Bright Vela supernova-remnant pulsar (89 ms).
First pulsar ever detected (Hewish + Bell 1967).
Nearest known millisecond pulsar (5.76 ms).
Magnetar famous for the 2004-12-27 giant flare (10⁴⁶ erg in 0.2 s).
Low-magnetic-field magnetar, quiescent source with sporadic outbursts.
Anomalous X-ray pulsar (AXP), confirmed magnetar in Carina.
Post-merger ~62 M☉ black hole from the first LIGO detection (2015-09-14).
Nearby γ-ray-loud, radio-quiet pulsar (237 ms period, age ~340 kyr).
First millisecond pulsar ever discovered (1982, 1.558 ms period).
Most massive precisely-measured neutron star (2.08 ±0.07 M☉).
Microquasar with superluminal jets, ~6 M☉ black hole primary.
Persistent soft-state black hole binary in the Large Magellanic Cloud.
Wolf-Rayet + ~30 M☉ BH binary in the starburst galaxy IC 10.
